number-to-words-converter.quickAnswer: Type a whole number and it is spelled out in words instantly — in the language you are browsing in. English uses thousand/million/billion, Hindi uses hazar/lakh/crore, and Arabic follows standard number grammar.
keyFacts: English groups digits in threes: thousand, million, billion, trillion.
Hindi uses the Indian system: hazar/thousand (1,000), lakh (1,00,000), crore (1,00,00,000).
Arabic has special dual and plural forms: alf (1000), alfaan (2000), aalaaf (3-10 thousand).
Writing amounts in words on cheques prevents tampering with digits.
This tool handles whole numbers from −999 trillion to 999 trillion.
howTo: Type a whole number into the input field (commas and spaces are ignored).
The words appear instantly below, in your current site language.
Switch the site language to get the words in English, Hindi or Arabic.
Use the formatted number row to double-check the digits.
Copy the words for cheques, invoices or documents.
number-to-words-converter.formula:
English: groups of three digits → hundred, thousand, million, billion, trillion.
Example: 1,234,567 = one million two hundred and thirty-four thousand five hundred and sixty-seven
number-to-words-converter.workedExample:
Convert 12345 to words.
English: 12 thousand + 345 → "twelve thousand three hundred and forty-five".
Hindi: 12 hazaar + 345 → "baarah hazaar teen sau paintaalees".
Arabic: 12 alf + 345 → "ithnaa ashara alfan wa thalaathu mi-ah wa khamsah wa arba-oon".
benefits: Three languages in one tool — English, Hindi and Arabic.
Hindi follows the Indian lakh/crore system correctly.
Arabic uses proper dual/plural grammar forms.
Handy for cheques, invoices, legal documents and schoolwork.
limitations: Whole numbers only — decimals like 12.5 are not spelled out.
Range is limited to safe integers below 1,000,000,000,000,000.
Arabic output is supported up to 999,999,999.
Currency names (rupees, dollars) are not added automatically.

faqs.q: How do you write 100000 in words in Hindi?
faqs.a: Ek laakh (one lakh). The Indian system groups as: 1,000 = ek hazaar, 1,00,000 = ek laakh, 1,00,00,000 = ek karod.

faqs.q: Why do cheques need the amount in words?
faqs.a: Words are much harder to alter than digits, so banks require the amount written out as a fraud check against the figures.
'Alf'. Two thousand is 'alfaan', 3-10 thousand uses 'aalaaf' (e.g. 'thalaathatu aalaaf'), and 11+ uses 'alfan' (e.g. 'ahada ashara alfan').

faqs.q: What is the largest number supported?
faqs.a: Up to 999,999,999,999,999 (999 trillion) in English and Hindi; Arabic is supported up to 999,999,999.
